correctness.rationale: On classical-only atomic valuations, each of the five propositional operations preserves {t,f}. By Definition 6, the eight b/n modalities of every classical operand reduce to t for the positive/negative essence variants and f for the positive/negative accident variants; none accesses values at other worlds. A structural induction proves pointwise locality for every restricted formula at arbitrary finite depth. On a two-world universal S5 frame, keeping all local atoms fixed and flipping p at the other world changes the truth component of each of the 16 t/f/T/F target modalities, as verified by direct case analysis. Therefore definability fails in each case. verify.py implements both truth/falsity clauses, tests all 32 classical exceptional-status cases and 16 target separations; finite tests corroborate but do not substitute for the induction. Scope explicitly excludes box/diamond and truth constants.

originality.rationale: The July 2026 journal paper explicitly poses the sixteen separations as Hypothesis 13 and gives definitions and positive transformations but no such proof. This result proves all sixteen simultaneously and rules out a stronger combined eight-operator defining language. Close literature, both journal and arXiv representations, related FDE definability work, and semantic record searches were compared at the level of implication rather than title resemblance; the existing related results do not visibly cover the stronger assertion. Residual risk from unavailable older full text and independently discovered work remains.
residual_risks: The 2019 definability paper was inspected at abstract and publisher-record level only after the original PDF endpoint was inaccessible; a previously known general nondefinability principle might resemble the classical-fragment technique.
Semantic literature searches cannot exclude unindexed, unpublished, or concurrent independent proofs.
The claim is specifically about formulas using no primitive necessity, possibility or nonclassical truth constants.

value.rationale: The result settles Hypothesis 13 explicitly raised in Petrukhin (2026), a motivated unanswered expressive-power question for newly introduced four-valued essence and accident operators. It proves the full 16-case statement plus a genuinely stronger mixed-family language barrier. The collapse lemma is structural and the two-point witnesses show that nonclassical truth values are not required to separate these modal operators; the result is not a numerical recomputation or a simple substitution of a pre-existing formula.
